title: The Catalan-triangle recurrence B(p,q) = B(p−1,q) + B(p,q−1) from the ballot closed form and Pascal's rule
description: Answers the parent entry's lead open question: derive the defining two-term recurrence of the Catalan triangle, ballot p q = ballot (p−1) q + ballot p (q−1) for 1 ≤ q ≤ p, directly from the parent's closed form ballot p q = C(p+q,q) − C(p+q,p+1) and Pascal's rule. The proof is pure binomial algebra: substituting p = a+1, q = b+1 makes every binomial index a clean polynomial in a,b; Pascal's rule Nat.choose_succ_succ' splits each of the two binomials of ballot p q into the two reduced-row coefficients; and the parent's ballot_genuine supplies the three genuineness bounds (C(p+q,p+1) ≤ C(p+q,q) and its shifts) that let the truncated ℕ-subtractions recombine — a single omega then closes the goal over the six binomial atoms. As a corollary, the diagonal recurrence ballot n n = ballot n (n−1) follows because the left neighbour ballot (n−1) n lies above the diagonal and vanishes (parent's ballot_eq_zero_of_lt). Together with the boundary ballot p 0 = 1, the recurrence regenerates the entire Catalan triangle row by row. Verified with 0 axioms, 0 sorries, no native_decide.

meta.author: Classical (Catalan triangle / Shapiro ballot table recurrence); Lean formalization original

mathlibDependencies.description: Pascal's rule in +1 form: choose (n+1) (k+1) = choose n k + choose n (k+1). Applied at (n,k) = (a+b+1, b) and (a+b+1, a+1) it splits the two binomials of ballot (a+1) (b+1) into the four coefficients of the reduced row a+b+1.

For q ≤ p, C(p+q,p+1) ≤ C(p+q,q): the genuineness of the ballot subtraction. Instantiated at (a+1,b+1), (a+1,b), and (a,b+1) it supplies the three ≤-bounds that keep every ℕ-subtraction in the recurrence exact, so omega can recombine them.
p < q ⇒ ballot p q = 0 (above the diagonal). Used in the diagonal corollary: ballot (n−1) n = 0 collapses the two-term recurrence to ballot n n = ballot n (n−1).

originalContributions: ballot_recurrence: ballot p q = ballot (p−1) q + ballot p (q−1) for 1 ≤ q ≤ p — the defining additive law of the Catalan triangle, derived directly from the parent's closed form and Pascal's rule (this is the parent entry's lead open question openQuestions[2]).

Proof technique: substitute p = a+1, q = b+1 to clear the predecessors and normalise indices; apply Pascal's rule Nat.choose_succ_succ' to each of the two binomials of ballot p q; supply three genuineness bounds from the parent's ballot_genuine (covering the diagonal edge q = p as an equality); then close the linear ℕ-relation among the six binomial coefficients with a single omega — no path counting, no real-valued probability.

ballot_recurrence_diag: ballot n n = ballot n (n−1) for n ≥ 1 — the edge rule carrying the Catalan numbers up the diagonal, since the left neighbour ballot (n−1) n vanishes above the diagonal (parent's ballot_eq_zero_of_lt).
Three concrete kernel-decide sanity checks of the recurrence: B(4,2) = B(3,2) + B(4,1) (9 = 5+4), the diagonal B(3,3) = B(3,2) (5 = 5), and B(5,3) = B(4,3) + B(5,2).

overview.historicalContext: The Catalan triangle (Shapiro's ballot table) has entries B(p,q) counting monotone lattice paths from (0,0) to (q,p) that stay weakly below the main diagonal. Like Pascal's triangle, it is generated by a two-term additive recurrence B(p,q) = B(p−1,q) + B(p,q−1): an entry is the sum of its left and lower neighbours, the lattice-path decomposition by the last step. The boundary B(p,0) = 1 and the recurrence together fill the whole triangle, and the diagonal carries the Catalan numbers B(n,n) = catalan n. This entry derives that recurrence arithmetically from the parent entry's reflection closed form, closing the circle between the explicit formula and the inductive rule.
overview.problemStatement:
The parent entry catalan-numbers-oq-01-oq-01-oq-02 proves the ballot closed form B(p,q) = C(p+q,q) − C(p+q,p+1) and asks (openQuestions[2]) to derive the Catalan-triangle recurrence B(p,q) = B(p−1,q) + B(p,q−1) (for q ≤ p) directly from that closed form and Pascal's rule, exhibiting the full triangle structure.

**Answer:** ballot_recurrence establishes exactly this for 1 ≤ q ≤ p, and ballot_recurrence_diag specializes it to the diagonal edge rule ballot n n = ballot n (n−1).
overview.text: A pure ℕ-binomial proof: clear the predecessors with p = a+1, q = b+1, split the two binomials of the closed form by Pascal's rule, and let the parent's genuineness bounds recombine the truncated subtractions under a single omega.
overview.proofStrategy:
1. Substitute p = a+1 and q = b+1 (licensed by 1 ≤ q ≤ p), so p−1 = a, q−1 = b, and every binomial index becomes a polynomial in a,b after simp [Nat.add_sub_cancel].
2. Pascal's rule (Nat.choose_succ_succ') at (a+b+1, b) and (a+b+1, a+1) gives C(a+b+2,b+1) = C(a+b+1,b) + C(a+b+1,b+1) and C(a+b+2,a+2) = C(a+b+1,a+1) + C(a+b+1,a+2): the two binomials of ballot (a+1)(b+1) split into the reduced row a+b+1.
3. Three genuineness bounds from the parent's ballot_genuine: C(a+b+2,a+2) ≤ C(a+b+2,b+1) at (a+1,b+1); C(a+b+1,a+2) ≤ C(a+b+1,b) at (a+1,b); and C(a+b+1,a+1) ≤ C(a+b+1,b+1) at (a,b+1) for b < a, with the diagonal case b = a holding as an equality (le_refl). These keep all three ℕ-subtractions exact.
4. Rewrite the goal to the normalized binomial indices (defeq) and close with omega over the six coefficient atoms X = A+B, Y = C+D, Y ≤ X, C ≤ B, D ≤ A ⊢ X − Y = (B − C) + (A − D).
5. ballot_recurrence_diag: specialize at p = q = n; ballot (n−1) n = 0 by ballot_eq_zero_of_lt (n−1 < n), so the recurrence collapses to ballot n n = ballot n (n−1).
keyInsights: **The recurrence is Pascal's rule, reflected.** ballot p q = C(p+q,q) − C(p+q,p+1) is a difference of two binomials; applying Pascal's rule to each and regrouping yields exactly ballot (p−1) q + ballot p (q−1). The Catalan-triangle recurrence is the difference of two copies of Pascal's recurrence.

**Clearing predecessors removes all truncated subtraction from the indices.** Writing p = a+1, q = b+1 turns p−1, q−1, p+1 into honest sums a, b, a+2, so Pascal's rule and the genuineness lemma apply on the nose and omega never has to reason about index truncation — only about the value-level subtractions, which the genuineness bounds make exact.

**The diagonal edge is the recurrence with a vanishing neighbour.** On the diagonal the left neighbour ballot (n−1) n sits strictly above the diagonal of its own row and is 0, so B(n,n) = B(n,n−1): the rule that propagates catalan n = B(n,n) up the triangle's edge is a special case of the two-term recurrence, not a separate fact.

**Genuineness covers the diagonal as an equality.** The one bound not directly furnished by ballot_genuine (the q = p case of the left neighbour) holds because the two binomial indices coincide there — the proof splits b < a (Pascal genuineness) from b = a (reflexivity), so the single omega works uniformly across the closed regime 1 ≤ q ≤ p.

exampleSections.title: Reading the recurrence off the triangle
exampleSections.mathContext: Off the diagonal, B(4,2) = 9 decomposes as B(3,2) + B(4,1) = 5 + 4: the paths to (2,4) weakly below the diagonal split by whether the last step is up (from (2,3), counted by B(3,2)) or right (from (1,4), counted by B(4,1)). On the diagonal the left neighbour drops out: B(3,3) = 5 = B(3,2), since B(2,3) = 0 lies above the diagonal — the edge rule that carries catalan 3 = 5 up the triangle. A deeper row: B(5,3) = B(4,3) + B(5,2).

sections.title: The two-term Catalan-triangle recurrence
sections.summary: ballot_recurrence: for 1 ≤ q ≤ p, ballot p q = ballot (p−1) q + ballot p (q−1). After clearing predecessors with p = a+1, q = b+1, Pascal's rule (Nat.choose_succ_succ') splits the two binomials of ballot p q, three genuineness bounds from the parent's ballot_genuine (the diagonal case b = a held by reflexivity) keep all ℕ-subtractions exact, and omega closes the six-atom linear identity.

sections.title: The diagonal edge recurrence
sections.summary: ballot_recurrence_diag: ballot n n = ballot n (n−1) for n ≥ 1. The left neighbour ballot (n−1) n lies above the diagonal and vanishes (parent's ballot_eq_zero_of_lt), collapsing the two-term recurrence to the edge rule that carries the Catalan numbers up the triangle.

conclusion.summary: The Catalan-triangle recurrence ballot p q = ballot (p−1) q + ballot p (q−1) holds for 1 ≤ q ≤ p (ballot_recurrence), with the diagonal edge rule ballot n n = ballot n (n−1) as a corollary (ballot_recurrence_diag). Both are derived purely arithmetically from the parent's reflection closed form and Pascal's rule, with the truncated ℕ-subtractions recombined by the parent's genuineness bounds under a single omega. Verified with 0 axioms, 0 sorries, no native_decide.
conclusion.implications: Closes the loop between the explicit ballot closed form and the inductive structure of the Catalan triangle: the same difference of two binomials that defines B(p,q) satisfies Pascal's two-term recurrence, so the triangle can be generated either by the reflection formula or row by row from the boundary B(p,0) = 1 — and the Catalan numbers ride up its diagonal edge.
openQuestions: Bijective recurrence: realize ballot p q = ballot (p−1) q + ballot p (q−1) as the last-step decomposition of lattice paths (up vs right), matching the arithmetic identity to an explicit bijection of path sets.

Full-triangle induction: use the recurrence plus the boundary B(p,0) = 1 to give an independent inductive proof of the closed form B(p,q) = C(p+q,q) − C(p+q,p+1), closing the equivalence of the two characterizations.
